root_cause.text: The function parse_apply_sb_mount_options() used strscpy_pad() to copy a fixed-size (64-byte) superblock field `s_mount_opts` that may lack a NUL terminator, causing a buffer over-read when strscpy_pad() scans past the source buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch reduces the destination buffer from 65 to 64 bytes (matching `s_mount_opts` size) and adds a check `if (strscpy_pad(s_mount_opts, sbi->s_es->s_mount_opts) < 0) return -E2BIG;`. The CVE description warns of a "65 byte read of buffer size 64" triggered by strscpy_pad when the source is not NUL-terminated, and states that "userspace is expected to provide s_mount_opts field to be at most 63 characters long with the ending byte being NUL-term" – thus a full 64-character non-terminated string causes the over-read. The commit message explicitly says "strscpy_pad() can't be used to copy a non-NUL-term string into a NUL-term string of possibly bigger size."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixed buffer size off-by-one in parse_apply_sb_mount_options by reducing the s_mount_opts array from 65 to 64 bytes to match the intended maximum length.
intent_record.what: Changed the size of the local character array `s_mount_opts` from 65 to 64 in the function `parse_apply_sb_mount_options` in fs/ext4/super.c.
intent_record.how: This reduces the buffer size by one byte, affecting the maximum length of mount options string that can be stored. If the previous size was intended for a 64-character string plus null terminator (65 bytes), the new size would only accommodate 63 characters plus null, or it corrects a previous off-by-one error to match a 64-byte field.

intent_record.intent_summary: Check return value of strscpy_pad when copying mount options and return -E2BIG if the source is too large, preventing silent truncation.
intent_record.what: Added a return value check for strscpy_pad; if it returns negative, the function returns -E2BIG.
intent_record.how: Prevents silent truncation of mount options by aborting the function when the source string exceeds the destination buffer capacity.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adjusts the destination buffer size from 65 to 64 bytes, but does not address the core issue of the source string lacking a NUL terminator, which causes the buffer over-read in strscpy_pad().

The group adds a check for the return value of strscpy_pad() to detect when the source lacks a NUL terminator (causing -E2BIG), which directly prevents the buffer over-read described in the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: strscpy_pad reads from the source buffer until it finds a NUL terminator; if the superblock field s_mount_opts is not NUL-terminated (e.g., because it was written with strncpy without null termination), strscpy_pad will read beyond the 64-byte field, causing a buffer over-read.
